title: Perinatal Taurine Supplementation Prevents Metabolic and Cardiovascular Effects of Maternal Dyslipidemia in Adult Rat Offspring

sections.abstract: <jats:p>Maternal obesity predisposes metabolic and cardiovascular disorders in adult offspring. This study tests the hypothesis that perinatal taurine supplementation prevents dyslipidemia and hypertension in adult offspring of dyslipidemic rat mothers. Female Wistar rats were fed normal rat chow and water with (Dyslipidemia group) or without dyslipidemic induction by intraperitoneal Triton WR‐1339 injection (Control group). After confirmed pregnancy, they were supplemented with (Control+T and Dyslipidemia+T) or without 3% taurine in water from conception to weaning. After weaning, male offspring were fed normal rat chow and water throughout the study. At 16 weeks of age, body weight, epididymis fat size, fasting blood glucose (Control, 84 ± 2 mg/dl; Control+T, 85 ± 3 mg/dl; Dyslipidemia, 96 ± 2 mg/dl; Dyslipidemia+T, 82 ± 2 mg/dl; P < 0.05), plasma low‐density lipoprotein (Control, 102 ± 6 mg/dl; Control+T, 100 ± 6 mg/dl; Dyslipidemia, 137 ± 7 mg/dl; Dyslipidemia+T, 107 ± 5 mg/dl; P < 0.05) and cholesterol (Control, 81 ± 5 mg/dl; Control+T, 81 ± 3 mg/dl; Dyslipidemia, 95 ± 3 mg/dl; Dyslipidemia+T, 81 ± 2 mg/dl; P < 0.05), mean arterial pressure, and heart rate increased but baroreflex sensitivity decreased significantly in Dyslipidemia compared to Control groups. While perinatal taurine supplementation did not affect these parameters in the Control, this treatment normalized, at least in part, the metabolic and cardiovascular effects of maternal dyslipidemia in adult offspring. In addition, plasma high‐density lipoprotein, triglyceride, leptin, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, creatinine, and blood urea nitrogen were not significantly different among the four groups, irrespective of maternal dyslipidemia or taurine supplementation. These data demonstrate that perinatal taurine supplementation prevents the adverse effects of maternal dyslipidemia on metabolic and cardiovascular defects in adult male offspring.</jats:p> <jats:p> <jats:bold>Support or Funding Information</jats:bold> </jats:p> <jats:p>Suranaree University of Technology</jats:p>
